body:
The app should notice when the server carries a newer APK than the installed one and
offer to update -- once per version, never nagging twice for the same one.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-android-update-check-design.md

Server: unauthenticated GET /api/v1/app-version returning the package version and the
absolute APK URL. Registered ONLY when the APK is actually served, reusing routes/apk.py's
graceful degradation -- so a server without the Android artifact, and every server released
before this feature, simply 404s and the client stays quiet.

Client: check on foreground, rate-limited to once per 12h; semver-compare the server's
version against BuildConfig.VERSION_NAME; prompt once per version; "Update" hands off to
the system with ACTION_VIEW on the APK URL (no new permissions, no in-app download).
Settings gains a device-local "check automatically" switch, default on, below the
notification switch -- off means no request at all.

Not verifiable in this sandbox: that ACTION_VIEW actually reaches a browser and the
install completes. Device-only, and the riskiest part of the feature.
title: Android: in-app update check with a per-device opt-out
